$$\begin{cases} x + 2y = 13 \\ 4x - y = 7 \end{cases}$$
hints: Cramer's rule: $x = \dfrac{\det A_x}{\det A}$ and $y = \dfrac{\det A_y}{\det A}$, where $A_x$ (resp. $A_y$) is $A$ with its first (resp. second) column replaced by the right-hand side.
Compute $\det A$ first; if it is zero, Cramer's rule does not apply.

Replace column 2 of $A$ with the constants: $A_y = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 13 \\ 4 & 7 \end{pmatrix}$, so $\det A_y = -45$.

hints: Cramer's rule: $x = \dfrac{\det A_x}{\det A}$ and $y = \dfrac{\det A_y}{\det A}$, where $A_x$ (resp. $A_y$) is $A$ with its first (resp. second) column replaced by the right-hand side.
Compute $\det A$ first; if it is zero, Cramer's rule does not apply.
solution_steps_latex: Form the coefficient matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -2 \\ 4 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$ and compute $\det A = (-1)(-1) - (-2)(4) = 9$.
Replace column 1 of $A$ with the constants: $A_x = \begin{pmatrix} -8 & -2 \\ -4 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$, so $\det A_x = 0$.
Replace column 2 of $A$ with the constants: $A_y = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -8 \\ 4 & -4 \end{pmatrix}$, so $\det A_y = 36$.
